CommitmentAthlete.description:
The athlete, as the best-ranked source that lists them gives it. Most
are high-school students: contact details, dates of birth and social
accounts are never collected, so they are never here.

club.description: Club team, where the source names one.
club.title: Club

grad_year.description: High-school graduation class. Null where the sources give only the college entry year (see `entry_year`).

Null when there is no `high_school` text or it has not been classified yet. `high_school` itself is always the text the source printed.
high_school_kind.title: High School Kind

person_id.description: The athlete's id, from the moment they commit: the same id on every commitment they make (a decommitment and a recommitment elsewhere share it), and the `person_id` their player record carries once they enroll, across transfers. All of an athlete's commitments: GET /v1/commitments?person_id=. In the rare case two ids turn out to be one athlete, the ids are merged: the commitment then carries the surviving id (a `commitment.updated`), and the other keeps resolving to it. Null only in the last form of a commitment retracted because its athlete record was removed.
person_id.title: Person Id

player_id.description: Set once the class has enrolled and the athlete is on the committed team's roster: GET /v1/players/{player_id}. A player id is one roster stint; `person_id` is the athlete.
player_id.title: Player Id

position.description: As the recruiting source prints it ('MF', 'CM', 'ATH'); sources differ. Read `positions` and `position_groups` for one value per sport.
position.title: Position

position_groups.description: The broadest category of each of `positions`: baseball 'SS' is in 'INF', 'RHP' in 'P'; basketball 'PG' in 'GUARD'; ice hockey 'LW' in 'F'; football 'OT' in 'OL'. A sport whose vocabulary is flat (soccer, volleyball, lacrosse, field hockey) repeats `positions`. Null or [] exactly where `positions` is. Read the same way as `positions`.
position_groups.title: Position Groups

positions.description: The standardized position or positions `position` names, in the sport's canonical vocabulary: the values GET /v1/filters/catalog lists for the player `position` field ('GK', 'DEF', 'MID', 'FWD' in soccer; 'PG', 'SS', 'OH', 'QB', ...). A list because a school can print two: soccer 'M/F' is ['MID', 'FWD']. Each value is one you can filter by, and a `position` filter matches the row by the same reading, so a player returned for `position=FWD` carries 'FWD' here. Null for a sport with no positions (tennis, golf, swimming and diving, track and field); [] where the sport has them and the published text names none (nothing published, a role such as 'Special Teams', a spelling not yet in the vocabulary). Read from the commitment's sport and `position` when the commitment is served or sent, the same on a GET and in a webhook: a vocabulary change reaches every commitment at once, without a revision or a `commitment.updated`.
positions.title: Positions

secondary_school.description: The registry school `high_school` names, when `high_school_kind` is 'high_school'; null otherwise. Read when the commitment is built: a school linked or corrected later shows here without a new revision or a `commitment.updated`. Filter by it with `high_school_nces_id`.

info.description:
REST API for college sports data across NCAA D1/D2/D3, NAIA, and NJCAA:
players, teams and schools, rosters and coaching staffs, cross-program
careers, games, roster and staff movements, the live transfer portal, and an
agent-backed natural-language query endpoint.

## Authentication

Every endpoint requires an API key sent as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer mag_live_...
```

Create and manage keys in the developer console at
[magisterial.ai/console/api-keys](https://magisterial.ai/console/api-keys).
Keys are prefixed `mag_live_` (production) or `mag_test_` (the sandbox: see
[Sandbox](#sandbox)).

Every key also carries an exact delegated capability list. A key's effective
authority is the intersection of those scopes with the actor's current role,
verification, account plan, and requested sport. Scope names do not imply one
another by prefix. New keys default to the non-PII `chat.use` scope.

## Scoping

Data access is scoped by `sport`, `division`, and (for dual-gender sports)
`gender`. `GET /v1/sports` lists every sport with its genders and the
divisions each gender is offered in, and `GET /v1/divisions?sport=...` returns
one sport's list. Divisions differ by sport (football has `D1-FBS` and
`D1-FCS`, men's volleyball has no `NWAC`), so build a scope from the sport's
own list: any non-empty comma-separated subset of it is valid, e.g.
`D1,NAIA,NJCAA-D1`. Football's `D1` is the combined view of `D1-FBS` and
`D1-FCS`; request the combined code or the subdivisions, not both.

A query parameter an endpoint does not accept is refused with 400
`unknown_parameter`, and the error lists what the endpoint accepts. A filter
is never silently ignored.

## Names

A player's `name` is in natural order (`Jordan Rivera`) on every player,
roster, transfer-portal, movement and managed-athlete record. `first_name`
and `last_name` are set when the roster source published the name in split
form and null when it published one undivided name. Box-score and
play-by-play lines inside `GET /v1/games/{game_id}` carry each name as the
game source printed it; use the line's `player_id` for the player record.

## School identity discovery

Use `POST /v1/schools/resolve` with `kind=college`, one whole `query`, and
`sport`, `gender`, `division` to identify a college. For example,
`{"kind":"college","query":"Lock Haven University","sport":"soccer","gender":"women","division":"D2"}`.
Canonical names and aliases return `selected`; partial or typo matches return
ranked `candidates` with location, external IDs and available program IDs.
Choose using your user's context, then persist the college `school_id` or
program `team_id`. Identity is found before checking program scope: a known
institution without this sport/division returns its identity and empty
`in_scope_team_ids`, never a similar in-scope institution.

`GET /v1/teams?school=...` and `POST /v1/players/search` with `school` share
this contract and include `school_resolutions`. For player searches, a scalar
`school` is one whole name (including punctuation commas); an array is any-of.
Use `school_id: [1904]` or `team_id: [14306]` for subsequent player reads.
Separate filter fields intersect. Existing `/teams` `name` (exact) and `q`
(contains), player `high_school` (exact source text), and legacy player
`team_name` filters retain their meanings. `school` is the explicit migration
from legacy matching to identity discovery. Team-name arrays preserve complete
names; scalar legacy CSV is retained only when the whole name is not recognized.

For secondary schools, use `kind=high_school`, `query` and optional school
`city`, `state`, `country`, or explicit `high_school_id` / string `nces_id`.
Knoch and Knoch High School discover the same registry identity; Freeport
candidates include their states. School location is distinct from an athlete's
hometown. College `school_id`, college `team_id`, high-school `high_school_id`,
IPEDS UNITID and NCES ID are separate namespaces. Use the returned high-school
IDs with player/commitment attendance filters. Discovery is read-only; attendance
coverage depends on completed source-record linking.

## Using API data

On any paid API plan, you may use, store, modify, display, redistribute, and resell the data returned by the API, including in commercial products. No separate license, attribution, written permission, or Enterprise agreement is required.

Choose a plan for the data access, features, and usage limits you need.
Enterprise offers higher volumes, custom limits, and dedicated support.

## Data sources and freshness

Records are compiled from publicly available sources and from the people
they describe:

- **School athletics sites.** Rosters, coaching staffs, schedules, results,
  box scores, and season statistics come from each program's official
  athletics website (Sidearm Sports, Presto Sports, and WMT-hosted sites),
  read as published and normalized into one schema. `bio_url`,
  `boxscore_url`, and a school's `athletics_domain` point back at the source.
- **Public federations and registries.** stats.ncaa.org for play-by-play and
  shot charts, TFRRS for track and field and cross-country performances, the
  NCAA transfer-portal listings, and federal IPEDS / College Scorecard data
  for institution profiles and the `ipeds_unitid` join key.
- **The people themselves.** Coaches and athletes who claim their profile add
  and correct their own information; recruiting questionnaires and in-product
  use contribute verified contact and preference data that is exposed only
  under the contact capabilities described in the Managed athletes section.

Headshots and logos are served by reference from school athletics sites
(some through our image proxy).

Freshness is a property of each record, not of the API. Roster, coaching
staff, and team responses carry a `freshness` object (`observed_at`, when the
source page was last fetched; `changed_at`, when the content last changed;
`next_check_at`), and `GET /v1/coverage` lists the last run of every ingest
lane. For rosters and coaching staffs `changed_at` is when what this API
returns for the team's latest season last changed (a player added, removed or
edited in any returned field, a staff member added, removed or retitled),
whichever source the change came from. It is never earlier than the change
it reports, so to sync incrementally list `GET /v1/teams` with
`roster_changed_since` or `coaches_changed_since` set to the start of your
previous sync and re-read only those teams. A program's first `changed_at`
is when tracking began for it, not a change: every program holding a roster
or staff when tracking started carries that same first timestamp, so one full
read after it is the baseline. Tracking covers every association alike
(NCAA, NAIA, NJCAA, 3C2A, NWAC, NCCAA, USCAA); a change is seen when the
program's roster or staff lane next reads its source (the table below). Roster and coaching-staff responses also carry `coverage`, which says
what the list means: `held`, `season_not_held` (other seasons are held, not
the one requested), `none_listed` (the program's page was read and lists
nobody), `not_collected` (no source has been read for the program yet, so an
empty list says nothing about it), `not_sponsored`, or `discontinued`. A
team's `status` and `discontinued_at` say whether the program still competes;
`GET /v1/teams?status=active` lists only those that do. The refresh policy is
seasonal:

| Data | Inside its churn window | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| Rosters | every 24 hours | every 7 days |
| Coaching staffs | every 7 days (Mar 1 to Jun 30) | every 14 days |
| Season statistics | every 7 days in season | every 14 days |
| Schedules and box scores | every 24 hours, sport lanes every 4 to 6 hours in season | daily |
| Movements | observed at scrape time, identity resolution every 6 hours | published once confirmed |
| Commitments | each source read daily or weekly (`GET /v1/commitments/sources` says when) | in the feed within minutes of the read |
| Portal supply | the NCAA portal read several times a day | counted once a day, after 10:00 UTC |

Movement events carry both `observed_at` (when the roster or staff page
changed) and `published_at` (when the event was confirmed and entered the
feed). The published feed carries a transfer once it is resolved to the
transfer edge it made (the arrival at the new school and the departure from
the old one), a coach's move once it is resolved to the post at another
school they held the season before, and confirmed head-coach changes. A
departure with no known destination, a new hire with no known previous post,
and a link to a post that ended more than a season earlier are not published.
Enterprise keys can read the resolver stream directly with `status=resolved`
or `status=observed` on `GET /v1/movements`.

## Commitments

`GET /v1/commitments` (Premium and up) is the college commitment feed:
one athlete committed to one program, reconciled across every public source
that lists it, from the national recruiting trackers to the platforms where
athletes record their own commitments (which carry most of D2, D3, NAIA and
junior college). A commitment is published only once its program is
resolved to a team, so `team_id` always joins to `GET /v1/teams/{team_id}`.
Each commitment carries its `sources`, each source's own date and what that
date means (`announced`, `recorded`, `added` or `published`); `committed_on`
is the best of them and `first_reported_at` is when we first read it.
Sources that disagree about the program are separate commitments. A source
reporting a signing makes it `signed`; one reporting a decommitment, or
listing the athlete at another program, makes it `decommitted`. Ice hockey
trackers give the college entry year rather than a high-school class
(`entry_year`). Most athletes are high-school students: no contact details,
dates of birth or social accounts are collected.

`GET /v1/commitments/changes` is the change log (each commitment that is or
was published, in its current state, oldest change first; retractions carry
their reason), the `commitment.*` webhooks push the same changes, and
`GET /v1/commitments/sources` says what each source covers and when it was
last read.

## Portal supply

`GET /v1/portal/supply` (Developer Ultra and up) is the transfer portal
without names: one row per program and position group, holding counts.
`in_portal` is the program's entries on the market now, `in_portal_returning`
the part of those known not to be in their last season (the openings the
portal adds beyond graduation), and `signed_out` the entries that signed or
enrolled elsewhere this cycle. The position group is the roster position's
group in team sports and football, the event group from results in track
and field and in swimming and diving, and the dual-match lineup tier in
tennis. Golf has no positions; its entries, and any entry not linked to a
roster player, count in the program's row with `lane` null. No row carries a name, class year, entry date or per-person id, so
nothing joins to `GET /v1/portal` (which stays verified-coach only).

Counts are taken once a day. `GET /v1/portal/supply/changes` is the change
log, dated by the snapshot day rather than the moment anything changed, and
the `portal_supply.changed` webhook pushes the same changes.

## Short seasons

The record and stats on a team's season (`documents` on `GET /v1/teams/{team_id}`)
are counted from the games Magisterial holds, and a past season can hold fewer
games than the team played. Every season record carries a `schedule` object
that says so. `games_played` is how many completed games the team's own
published schedule counts toward its record for the season, as last read:
exhibitions, scrimmages and games the school marks as not counting are left
out, whether the page labels them or only its schedule data does.
`official_record` is the record the school gives over those games, from the
same read, and `games_held` is how many final games we hold for the team that
are not exhibitions for it. A game one school counts and the other calls an
exhibition is held for the first and not the second. Each season's games are
read in the division the team was in that season, so a program that has since
moved division keeps its earlier seasons.

When `status` is `partial`, `games_held` is below `games_played` by
`missing_games`, and the season's record and stats cover only the games held.
When it is `complete`, we hold exactly the games the school counts and
`record_from_held_games` equals `official_record`. When it is `inconsistent`,
`games_held` is above `games_played`, or equal to it with a different record:
a held game is not one the school counts, or a held result differs from the
school's, and `record_from_held_games` should not be shown as the season's
record. When it is `unverified` we have not read the team's schedule for that
season, so `games_played`, `missing_games` and `official_record` are null and
nothing says whether the season is complete. `official_record` is given for a
partial or inconsistent season too, with `official_record_source`
`school_schedule`; a schedule read before the school's record was captured has
`official_record` only when the season is complete, with
`official_record_source` `held_games`. `record_from_held_games` is the record
over the games held whatever the status. A season is short when `status` is
`partial`.

Each season's `overall_record` ('W-L' or 'W-L-T') is the record on the
season's document, and `overall_record_source` says where it comes from:
`school_page`, the record the school posts on its own athletics site, or
`held_games`, our tally of the games we hold. A season label is the calendar
year the season ends in: fall sports (soccer, football, women's volleyball,
field hockey) are the fall they are played in; winter and academic-year sports
(basketball, ice hockey, swimming and diving, tennis, golf) are labelled by the
year the school year ends, so `2024` is the 2023-24 season (a tennis or golf
season spans the fall and the spring); and spring sports (baseball, softball,
lacrosse, men's volleyball) are that spring.

## Schools and external identifiers

Every team carries a `school` object with our school id, a stable slug, the
school's athletics domain, and its federal IPEDS UNITID (`ipeds_unitid`)
where the institution is in the federal universe (about 87% of schools, and
93% of NCAA programs). `GET /v1/schools` lists institutions with a
`ipeds_unitid` lookup, and `GET /v1/schools/{school_id}` returns every program
a school fields across sports and divisions, so you can join on UNITID first
and fall back to name, state, and conference only for the remainder.

The two school endpoints also carry the institution's `profile` from the U.S.
Department of Education's College Scorecard (the federal IPEDS reporting it
publishes): admission rate, SAT and ACT 25th/75th percentiles, undergraduate
enrollment, published in-state and out-of-state tuition and fees, average net
price, six-year graduation and first-year retention rates, religious
affiliation, campus setting, and the top fields of study by degrees awarded,
with the release year in `data_year`. A null field means the institution did
not report that measure or it does not apply (no admission rate at an
open-admission college, no graduation rate at a two-year one, no religious
affiliation at a secular one); `profile` itself is null where no federal
profile is held. Average net price is what aided students pay after grants,
not the cost of attendance; GPA ranges and the full cost of attendance are not
provided. The `school` object embedded in teams is unchanged and carries no
profile. `GET /v1/schools` filters on `religious_affiliation`, admission rate
and undergraduate enrollment ranges as well as `control`.

## High schools

`high_school` is the text a source printed and is never changed. Beside it,
players (search rows, profiles, rosters) and a commitment's `athlete` carry
`high_school_kind`, what we classified that text as (`high_school`, `college`,
`club`, `homeschool`, `not_a_school`, or `unresolved`; null when there is no
text or it has not been classified yet), and `secondary_school`, the registry
school it names, only when the kind is `high_school`. Public schools are
identified by their NCES `nces_id` (NCESSCH), private schools by their PPIN;
a school outside the NCES registries, such as a Canadian one, has none and is
identified by `id`. `GET /v1/high-schools` looks schools up by name, state or
`nces_id`. `POST /v1/players/search` filters by `high_school_nces_id`,
`high_school_id` and `high_school_kind`, and `GET /v1/commitments` by
`high_school_nces_id`, so every spelling of a school's name finds its athletes.

## Coach contacts

Coach contact fields (`email` and `phone` on `GET /v1/teams/{team_id}/coaches`)
are returned in three cases. None of them is metered. When they are withheld
the response says why in `contacts_unavailable_reason`.

**Coach directory.** Coach email and phone are included with Developer Pro,
Developer Ultra and Enterprise. No separate approval is needed. When creating
your API key, enable the `coach.contact.directory_read` scope to include
these fields on `GET /v1/teams/{team_id}/coaches`. A coach who asked not to be contacted is still listed, with
`contact_opt_out` true and no contact fields. Contact fields are never part
of bulk exports.

**Your own verified claim.** A key whose owner is a verified player and carries
`outreach.coach.read` reads contacts for that athlete, as in the app.

**Managed athletes.** A platform that represents many athletes obtains the
backing per athlete. Invite a player profile with `POST /v1/athletes`; the
athlete receives an email at an address we can vouch for (their on-file
contact, their school .edu address, or the account that already claimed the
profile) and accepts on magisterial.ai, which also completes their verified
claim. From then on any key on the account that carries `outreach.coach.read`
may pass `on_behalf_of=<player_id>` to read coach contacts for that athlete.
Every such read is recorded in the athlete's access log, and athletes can
withdraw the authorization at any time; a revoked or unclaimed grant denies on
the next call. Requires the Enterprise plan and the `managed_athlete.manage`
key scope; seats default to 250 per account.

## Filtering

Every list endpoint filters the same way. Each endpoint's parameter list
names the fields it filters on; the forms are always these:

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `field=value` | Exact match. Text compares case-insensitively. |
| `field=a,b,c` | Any of the values. |
| `field_not=a,b` | None of the values. A row with no value for the field is left out too. |
| `field_min=`, `field_max=` | Inclusive range, for numbers and dates. |
| `q=text` | Name contains, case-insensitive. |
| `sort_by=`, `sort_order=` | Where a list has more than one useful order. |

Filters combine with AND. A parameter the endpoint does not declare returns
400 `unknown_parameter` together with the list it accepts, so a mistyped
filter never comes back as an unfiltered page.

`POST /v1/players/search` takes the same names in its JSON body, with arrays
in place of comma lists, and every season stat as a range under `stats`,
keyed by the stat fields `GET /v1/filters/catalog` lists for the sport:

```json
{"sport": "soccer", "division": "D3", "position": "Forward",
 "class_year_not": "Senior / Graduate", "stats": {"g": {"min": 10}}}
```

Position, class year and home state are published by each school in its own
words ('F', 'Fwd', 'Forward'; 'Jr.', 'Junior'; 'OH', 'Ohio'). A filter on one
of them matches every spelling of the value you give, so use the canonical
values from the filter catalog.

`GET /v1/filters/catalog` says how each field can be used. `search_ops` is
what `POST /v1/players/search` takes: `eq` and `in` are the field as one value
or an array, `neq` and `not_in` are `field_not`, `gte` and `lte` are
`field_min` and `field_max` (for a stat, `min` and `max` under `stats`).
`alert_ops` is the `op` values an alert predicate on the field accepts. Until
2027-01-12 the catalog also returns the keys it had before (`request_key`,
`manual_search_operators` and the others marked deprecated); they name
parameters of the Magisterial app's own search, which no /v1 endpoint accepts.

Schools and movements span sports, so they take no required scope: one
`school_id` on `GET /v1/movements` is that school's movements in every sport,
and `GET /v1/schools/{school_id}` lists every team it fields.

## Postman

A ready-made Postman collection of every endpoint, generated from this
specification, is served at
[`/v1/postman.json`](https://api.magisterial.ai/v1/postman.json). In Postman
choose Import, paste that URL, then set the collection variable `api_key` to
your key once; every request sends it as the bearer token.

## Pagination

List endpoints paginate with an opaque `cursor`. Pass the `next_cursor` from
one response as the `cursor` of the next request; `has_more` signals whether
another page exists.

## Errors

Every 4xx/5xx returns a JSON envelope:

```json
{ "error": { "type": "invalid_request", "code": "invalid_scope", "message": "..." } }
```

An error may carry more keys than those three: `unknown_parameter` adds
`unknown` and `allowed`, and `plan_required` adds `required_plan` and
`current_plan`.

A request that fails validation (422) uses the same envelope, with code
`validation_error` and an `error.fields` list naming each offending field.
Until 2027-01-12 it also carries FastAPI's `detail` list beside `error`.
Rate-limited responses (429) include `X-RateLimit-Limit`,
`X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, and `Retry-After` headers. A 429
`monthly_quota_exceeded` also carries the `X-Monthly-Quota-*` headers below.

## Player stats

A stat has one name everywhere. `GET /v1/filters/catalog` lists each sport's
stat fields (`stats_by_sport`), with a label and a type; those are the names
`POST /v1/players/search` filters and sorts by, and the names in every `stats`
object the API returns: a search row's `stats`, each entry of a player's
`stats_by_season`, `stats_totals`, and the stat columns of a players export.
Every stat field of the sport is present on every row; a stat the source did
not publish is null. Track and field has no season stats: a search row reports
the athlete's best mark in `track`, and a player's `track_bests` lists the best
per event.

A player row carries its profile fields at the top level under the names the
filters use (`home_state`, `jersey_number`, `height_inches`, `bats`, ...).

Until 2027-01-12 the three player endpoints also return what they returned
before: inside a search row's `stats`, copies of the profile fields and the
soccer keys `sh%`, `sog%`, `sv%`, `yc-rc` and `pg-pa`; and `season_stats` on a
player and on season history. Those responses carry `Deprecation` and `Sunset`
headers.

## Plans

Every key inherits its owner's Developer-API plan. Six plans exist:

| Plan | Price | Read limit | Monthly requests | Portal, query, alerts, exports | Included query usage | Coach directory |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0, every account | 10 / minute | 1,000 | Not available | None | No |
| Plus | $19.99 / month | 20 / minute | 25,000 | Available; portal and alerts usage-billed | $5 / month | No |
| Premium | $49.99 / month | 100 / minute | 100,000 | Available; portal and alerts usage-billed | $15 / month | No |
| Developer Pro | $99.99 / month | 300 / minute | 250,000 | Available; portal and alerts included | $40 / month | Included |
| Developer Ultra | $199 / month | 1,200 / minute | 1,000,000 | Available; portal and alerts included | $100 / month | Included |
| Enterprise | Contact sales | Custom (6,000 / minute default) | Unlimited | Available, custom ceilings | Custom | Included |

The `plan` value in responses and headers is `free`, `plus`, `premium`,
`developer` (Developer Pro), `ultra` (Developer Ultra) or `enterprise`.
A paid plan also pays for the account's chat in the Magisterial app, counted
against the same limits. It adds no coaching tier.

Developer Pro, Developer Ultra and Enterprise accounts can have a team (5, 20
and 100 people by default, the owner included). Every key held by someone on
the account runs on the account's plan, and the per-minute limits and the
monthly quota are counted once for the whole account. A key, and the alerts
and query runs made with it, stay its owner's own.

The free read endpoints (players, season stats, teams, schools, rosters,
coaches, games, careers, transfers, published movements, reference data) are on every plan at
the plan's limits. Every response carries `X-Magisterial-Plan`; plans with a
monthly quota add `X-Monthly-Quota-Limit`, `X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining` and
`X-Monthly-Quota-Reset` (Unix seconds of the next reset: 00:00 UTC on the 1st
of the month, not your billing date), and a capped account receives 429
`monthly_quota_exceeded`, with the same headers, until the UTC calendar month
rolls over. Plans and prices:
[magisterial.ai/pricing/developers](https://magisterial.ai/pricing/developers).
Upgrade in the developer console
([magisterial.ai/console/billing](https://magisterial.ai/console/billing));
Enterprise is arranged per customer.

## Billing

Endpoints marked *usage-billed* (`/v1/portal`, `/v1/query`, `/v1/alerts`,
`/v1/exports`) are open on every paid plan (a Free key receives 403
`plan_required`), require usage billing to be enabled on the account, and
meter usage against a monthly budget you set. List prices: exports $0.10 per
started 10,000-row block (billed on success only), and query at model cost
with a 3x markup, drawn first from the plan's included monthly query usage.
On Plus and Premium the portal is $0.05 per request and alerts are $5 per
active alert per month; from Developer Pro up both are included and only
count against the plan's request quota and alert cap. Buying a plan enables
usage billing on the same subscription. Billing-not-enabled and past-due states return 403; an exhausted monthly
budget returns 402.

Billing is additive, not authorization. In particular, `/v1/portal`, API
portal alerts (`/v1/alerts`, the `alert.triggered` webhook), portal answers
from `/v1/query` and the portal section of `/v1/filters/catalog` are bound to
a verified coach: the key must delegate the relevant portal capability and
the current actor must be an active, verified coach. No coaching plan is needed; the paid API plan covers
them. Enabling usage billing by itself never grants portal or athlete-contact
access. Athlete contacts require the separate `portal.contact.read` scope
under the same actor policy.

Movements are separate from the portal. `GET /v1/movements` and the movement
webhooks report roster and staff changes seen on school pages, and need no
coach verification on any plan.

## Bulk exports

For full-dataset pulls, use the bulk lane instead of walking paginated
endpoints: `POST /v1/exports` starts an async job that writes one dataset
(players, teams, games, or coaches) in one sport/division scope to a gzipped
CSV or JSONL file, and `GET /v1/exports/{export_id}` returns a short-lived
signed download URL once it succeeds. Billed on success by result size
(per started 10,000-row block); failed exports are never billed.

A players file ends with `positions` and `position_groups`, the standardized
reading of `position` that every other player object carries. In JSONL they
are arrays. In CSV a cell is the list as compact JSON (`["MID","FWD"]`), the
way a games file writes period scores. An empty CSV cell (null in JSONL) is a
sport with no position vocabulary (tennis, golf, swimming and diving, track and
field); `[]` is a sport that has one and a published position that names no
value in it. A players header only grows at its end, so these two columns come
after every column a file already had.

## Sandbox

A test key (`mag_test_`) reads a synthetic world instead of production: 24
invented schools in D1 and D3 with men's and women's soccer and basketball,
and everything the endpoints return for them (rosters, coaching staffs, games
with box scores, season statistics, rankings, postseason results, the transfer
portal and movements). No real person, school or address is in it, and its ids
sit far above any live id. Every response carries
`Magisterial-Environment: sandbox`.

Test keys are free. The usage-billed endpoints work without a paid plan or
billing, nothing is billed, and sandbox requests do not count toward the
monthly quota. Your plan's per-minute rate limits and the key's scopes still
apply, so what you build against a test key behaves the same with a live one.

`POST /v1/query` calls no model with a test key. It answers a short list of
sample questions from the sandbox data and answers anything else with a fixed
message that lists them. Exports and alerts run over the sandbox world.
`POST /v1/sandbox/events` makes something happen in it (a portal entry, an
athlete or a coach joining a program, a commitment published, updated or
retracted): your sandbox alerts are evaluated, and your registered webhook
endpoints receive the resulting events with `"test": true`. The commitment
feed (`GET /v1/commitments` and its change log and sources) is served from
invented high-school prospects committed to the sandbox's schools. Managed athletes are not available with a test key
(501 `sandbox_not_supported`).

## Webhooks

Instead of polling, register webhook endpoints in the
[console](https://magisterial.ai/console/webhooks) to receive signed events:
`alert.triggered` when a watch alert finds new portal matches, and
`query.completed` when an async query run finishes. Payloads carry a
`Magisterial-Signature` header (`t=<ts>,v1=<hmac_sha256_hex>` over
`{t}.{raw_body}`, keyed with the endpoint's `whsec_` secret); failed
deliveries retry with backoff for about two days. See the webhooks guide at
[magisterial.ai/docs](https://magisterial.ai/docs#webhooks-guide).

Developer Pro, Developer Ultra and Enterprise can also have the published
movement feed pushed: `coach_movement.published`, `coach_movement.updated`
and `coach_movement.retracted`, and the same three for `player_movement`.
Each event carries one movement, as the object `GET /v1/movements` returns,
with a per-movement `revision` that rises with every event. Apply them in
revision order and you hold what the published feed holds, corrections
included. Movement webhooks need no coach verification.

On every plan, `GET /v1/movements/changes` serves the same change log to a
consumer that polls: each movement that is or was published, in its current
state, oldest change first.

get.description:
Roster and coaching-staff movements, newest first. Cross-sport and
cross-division: no scope is required, and every filter is optional, so
`school_id=` alone is one school's movements in all of its sports. The
default `published` tier carries what is confirmed: a transfer once it is
resolved to the transfer it made (`transfer_id`), reported as the arrival
at the new school and the departure from the old one; a coach's move once
it is resolved to the post at another school they held the season before;
and confirmed head-coach changes. Each event is reported at the school the
person joined or left. Enterprise keys can read the resolver stream with
`status=resolved` (identity resolved, including departures with no known
destination and new hires with no known previous post) or
`status=observed` (every non-dismissed event, including pending ones),
each row carrying its `resolution_status` so you choose the confidence
threshold. `person_id` links into GET /v1/persons/{person_id};
`transfer_id` is the transfer edge a player movement minted.

To poll for new movements, keep the newest `published_at` you have seen,
pass it as `since` on the next call, and drop rows whose `kind` and `id`
you already hold (`since` is inclusive). That finds what was published,
not what changed afterwards: a correction leaves `published_at` as it
was, and a retracted movement is no longer returned at all. To keep a
copy of the feed correct, poll GET /v1/movements/changes instead. One
call returns players and coaches together unless `kind` is set. A
movement's key is (`kind`, `id`): ids are unique within a kind only.

get.description:
The change log of the published movement feed, oldest change first:
every movement that is or was in GET /v1/movements, in its current
state, ordered by when that state was last recorded. Polling it keeps a
copy of the feed correct, which polling GET /v1/movements by
`published_at` cannot: a movement that is corrected after publication
(its school, its counterpart, the person it is linked to) comes back
here with a higher `revision`, and one that is withdrawn comes back with
`state` 'retracted' and the `reason`.

To sync, read pages until `has_more` is false, then keep the last
entry's `changed_at` and pass it as `since` on the next poll (`since` is
inclusive, so expect that entry again). Apply each entry by
(`movement.kind`, `movement.id`): store `movement` when `state` is
'published', remove what you hold when it is 'retracted'. An entry is
the movement's latest state, not one event per change: a movement
corrected twice between two polls appears once, as it now stands. A
change to how a school is displayed (its name or logo) is not a
revision. A change is recorded here within about a minute of being
made. The movement webhooks deliver the same changes as they happen.

Who is in the transfer portal at each program, without saying who:
one row per program and position group, holding counts. `in_portal` is
on the market now, `in_portal_returning` the part of those known not to
be in their last season, and `signed_out` the ones who signed or
enrolled elsewhere this cycle. With the rosters (GET /v1/teams/{team_id}/roster)
and commitments (GET /v1/commitments) this is what you need to project
the spots opening at a program: departures from class year, plus
`in_portal_returning`, minus commitments.

No row names a player: there is no name, class year, entry date or
per-person id, so nothing here joins to GET /v1/portal or /v1/movements.
The position group is the roster position's group in team sports and
football, the event group from results in track and field and in
swimming and diving, and the dual-match lineup tier in tennis. Golf has
no positions; its entries, and any entry not linked to a roster player,
count in the program's row with `lane` null.

Counts are taken once a day. Rows are ordered by sport, program and
lane. To keep a copy current, read this once and then poll GET
/v1/portal/supply/changes, or subscribe to portal_supply.changed.

not say when a player entered. To sync, read pages until `has_more` is
false, keep the last entry's `changed_at`, and pass it as `since` on the
next poll (`since` is inclusive, so expect that day's entries again).

program's name or conference is not a revision. The portal_supply.changed

get.description:
What a team won and how far it went, season by season, in four
kinds of entry:

- `national_tournament`: every national championship tournament the
  team played in, with how far it went (`result`, `round`,
  `teams_remaining`), its seed, and its wins and losses there. NCAA
  tournaments are read from the NCAA's published brackets, NAIA
  championships from the NAIA's championship record books, and the
  College Football Playoff (organizer `CFP`) from the NCAA's scoreboard.
- `bowl_game`: an FBS bowl the team played in. `organizer` and `event`
  are the bowl, and `result` is `won` or `lost`. A playoff quarterfinal
  or semifinal played as a bowl is both a `CFP` entry and a `bowl_game`
  entry.
- `conference_regular_season`: a conference regular-season title.
- `conference_tournament`: a conference tournament (or championship
  game) the team won, or lost the final of where the conference names
  the runner-up.

Conference titles are read only from each conference's own list of its
champions, never worked out from standings. `shared` marks a title the
conference gave to more than one team, and `conference_division` a
title of a division inside the conference.

`coverage` lists the competitions and seasons held for the team: the
national tournaments of its sport and division, and the titles of the
conference it was in each season. Inside them, a season with no entry is
one the team did not play in the tournament, or did not win the title;
outside them, nothing is held either way. `division` may be omitted:
the team is read in its own current division. A team outside a division
that is given is a 404 naming the one it is in.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

422.description: The request failed validation; `error.fields` names each field.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. See the X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After headers; a monthly quota 429 also carries X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset.

tags.description: Teams, rosters, coaching staffs, and per-season team records, each with record-level freshness.
tags.name: Teams

tags.description: Institutions behind the teams, with the federal IPEDS UNITID for joining to external records and every program a school fields.
tags.name: Schools

tags.description: Cross-program careers and transfer histories, spanning divisions.
tags.name: Persons

tags.description: Roster and coaching-staff movements. The default feed carries what is confirmed (transfers resolved to their transfer edge, coach moves resolved to the post held the season before, head-coach changes); Enterprise keys can read the resolved and observed resolver tiers. Developer Pro and up can have the published feed pushed as webhooks.
tags.name: Movements

tags.description: College commitments reconciled across every public recruiting source, with a change log, the source catalog and commitment.* webhooks. Premium and up.
tags.name: Commitments

tags.description: The transfer portal as counts per program and position group, with no one named, and its daily change log and portal_supply.changed webhook. Developer Ultra and up; no coach verification.
tags.name: Portal Supply

tags.description: Games with box scores and play-by-play where covered.
tags.name: Games

tags.description: Golf has no games: its events are tournaments. Tournaments with team standings and every player's round scores, and magisterial's golf ratings.
tags.name: Golf

tags.description: Swimming & diving has no games: its events are meets. Meets, their results by event (times to the millisecond, splits, relay legs, dive scores), and an athlete's times.
tags.name: Swimming & Diving

tags.description: Individual singles and doubles matches from tournaments, and the ITA's individual rankings. Team duals and their lines are games (see Games).
tags.name: Tennis

tags.description: The live NCAA transfer portal feed. Requires a paid plan (usage-billed on Plus and Premium) and an active verified coach with exact delegated portal scopes. No coaching plan is needed.
tags.name: Transfer Portal

tags.description: Agent-backed natural-language questions over the data. Usage-billed.
tags.name: Query

tags.description: Standing transfer-portal watches: matches push to registered webhook endpoints (alert.triggered) or poll on demand. Requires a paid plan (usage-billed monthly on Plus and Premium) and an active verified coach, as the portal feed does. No coaching plan is needed.
tags.name: Alerts

tags.description: Async bulk exports: one dataset per job, gzipped CSV/JSONL, signed download URL. Usage-billed by size.
tags.name: Exports

tags.description: Test keys only: make something happen in the synthetic sandbox world so alerts and webhooks fire.
tags.name: Sandbox

tags.description: Enterprise only: invite athletes to authorize your platform, then read coach contacts on their behalf with on_behalf_of. Every delegated read is recorded in the athlete's access log. The coach directory itself is on Developer Pro and up (see the Coach contacts section).
tags.name: Managed athletes
